question: If a cosθ – b sinθ = c, then find the value of a sinθ + b cosθ.
solution:
**Given:**

a cosθ – b sinθ = c

**Concept used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

sin²θ + cos2​θ = 1

**Calculation:**

a cosθ – b sinθ = c

On squaring both sides, we get, a²cos2​θ + ​b²sin2​θ - 2ab × sinθ × cosθ = c²

⇒ a2(1 - sin2​θ) + ​b2(1 - cos2​θ) - 2ab × sinθ × cosθ = c²

⇒ a2 - a2sin2​θ + ​b2 - b2cos2​θ - 2ab × sinθ × cosθ = c2

⇒ a2 + ​b2 - c² = a2sin2​θ + b2cos2​θ + 2ab × sinθ × cosθ

⇒ a2 + ​b2 - c2 = (a sin​θ + b cos​θ)² 

⇒ a sin​θ + b cos​θ = ± sqrt{a² + b² - c²}
